h1: The 8 Best Microwaves for Dorm Rooms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Microwaves for Dorm Rooms: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 compact microwaves for dorm rooms compared on 700W output, mute buttons, presets and footprint, from COMFEE' to Toshiba.
summary: The COMFEE' 0.7 cu ft is the best dorm microwave: 700W, a mute function, ECO mode and a compact body. The Chefman with six food presets is the pick for first-time cooks. The Toshiba 900W heats fastest but may break dorm wattage rules.
intro: A dorm microwave faces three tests that a kitchen model never does. It has to fit a shelf or fridge top, it has to stay under whatever wattage the housing office allows, and it must not wake a roommate at one in the morning. Listings cover the first two sometimes and the third almost never, which is why the mute button is the feature that separates a good dorm pick from a merely small one.

We reviewed eight compact microwaves, seven at 0.7 cubic feet and 700W and one larger 900W unit, and ranked them on footprint, wattage, mute and safety features, and control simplicity. Housing rules vary by school, so treat wattage limits as something to confirm before you click buy, whatever the listing says.

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven (0.7 Cu.Ft, Standard)
products.verdict: 700W, a mute function and ECO mode in a small body. The easiest dorm pick.
products.description:
This COMFEE' is a 0.7 cu ft, 700W microwave with ECO mode and a mute function, in the $50 to $100 range. The mute function is the dorm-specific advantage. Beeps travel through thin walls, and a button that silences them means a midnight reheat will not wake a sleeping roommate. The 700W rating also fits the wattage limit that many housing offices set.

It wins because it covers every dorm basic in a compact body that moves in and out each semester. The Pearl White version costs more for identical specs, and the Chefman adds presets but costs about the same.

Buy it for a standard dorm. The caveats are a basic control panel and a small cavity that can pinch large plates. Check your housing wattage limit anyway.
products.idealFor: Students who want a no-fuss dorm microwave.

products.name: Chefman Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu. Ft.
products.verdict: 700W with ten power levels, six food presets, a child lock and a mute button.
products.description:
The Chefman 0.7 offers 700 watts with 10 power levels, six food-labeled presets, an eco mode, a child safety lock and a mute button, in the $50 to $100 range. Ten power levels matter more than they sound. They let you simmer or defrost gently, instead of blasting leftovers at full power until the edges turn rubbery.

It ranks just behind the COMFEE' because the price is about the same and the extra presets are a convenience rather than a necessity. It beats the Chefman Compact by offering six presets against three.

Buy it for a first-time dorm cook who wants labeled buttons for popcorn or pizza. Skip it if you want a larger cavity, because the cavity is small. The styling is basic, so expect function to outweigh form on a dorm shelf.

products.name: Farberware 0.7 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: The least expensive pick, with 700W, auto cook settings and multi-stage cooking.
products.description:
The Farberware lists 700 watts, auto cook settings, defrost, an easy-clean interior, a child safety lock and multi-stage cooking, in the $50 to $100 range. Multi-stage cooking chains cycles, for example a defrost step that rolls into a cook step, so frozen food gets treated gently before it heats.

It ranks third because the listing includes no mute function, which is the main thing dorm residents need after a wattage cap. It beats the Frigidaire on price, and its interior is easy to wipe down after a messy reheat. The white finish shows marks over time.

Buy it if budget is the tightest limit and you can live with beeps. Skip it if you share a room with a light sleeper. Compare it against the COMFEE' before you decide, since the mute feature is worth the small difference.

products.name: FRIGIDAIRE EMW733BLACKAMZ 0.7 Cu. Ft. Microwave
products.verdict: A delayed start and two defrost timers in a 700W body.
products.description:
The Frigidaire EMW733BLACKAMZ is a 0.7 cu ft, 700W microwave with a delayed start and two defrost timers, in the $50 to $100 range. Delayed start lets you queue a cook cycle to begin later, which helps when class schedules mean you want food ready the moment you walk in. Two defrost timers give more control than a single catch-all button.

It ranks fourth because delayed start is a niche feature and the listing leaves out a mute button. Compared with the Farberware, it gives you more control over timing, but fewer presets.

Buy it if your schedule is irregular and you like to time meals. Skip it if you want a mute button, since it is the quiet feature most dorm owners miss. Check the listing details, because our data on this model is sparse.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu.Ft, 700W
products.verdict: A fingerprint-resistant black finish and multi-stage cooking at 700W.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER lists a fingerprint-resistant black finish, multi-stage cooking, a child safety lock and 700W output at 0.7 cu ft, in the $50 to $100 range. A fingerprint-resistant surface sounds trivial until a shared suite has six people touching the door handle each day.

It ranks fifth because it lacks a mute function, the same gap as the Farberware and Frigidaire. Its edge is looks: the black finish hides the smudges that show on the white models, and the plain control panel is easy to read.

Buy it for a shared suite where appearance counts and several people use the same appliance. Skip it if you want a mute button. The COMFEE' and both Chefman units cost about the same and offer one, which matters more at night than a clean door.

products.name: Chefman Compact Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu. Ft.
products.verdict: Three focused presets, 10 power levels and a mute button. Simple for roommates.
products.description:
The Chefman Compact lists 700W with 10 power levels, two defrost settings, three focused presets, a child safety lock and a mute button, in the $50 to $100 range. Three presets are enough for the jobs a dorm microwave does most: popcorn, a reheat and a defrost.

It ranks sixth because the larger Chefman has six presets and the same wattage. The panel is plain enough that a new roommate can use it on the first try, which makes it suited to shared use. Both Chefman units share the 10 power levels and mute button.

Buy it if you share a microwave and want simple, quiet operation. Skip it if you want more presets. The small cavity is the real limit: a large bowl will not turn freely, so measure your dishes before ordering.
cons: Fewer presets than the other Chefman

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven (Pearl White)
products.verdict: The same COMFEE' in pearl white, at a higher price.
products.description:
This COMFEE' has the same mute function, ECO mode and 700W output as the standard model, in a pearl white finish, in the $50 to $100 range. The footprint and features match, so nothing changes in how it performs.

It ranks seventh because it costs more for the same specs. The finish is the only difference, and white shows stains from splatters and fingerprints faster than black does. If both versions were the same price it would sit higher, but the standard COMFEE' gives the identical dorm basics for less.

Pick it only if you want white to match your room and are happy to pay a little more. Skip it if price matters more than color. A bit of care keeps white looking clean, but it will take more wiping than the black model.
cons: Costs more for the same specs

products.name: TOSHIBA Microwave Oven (0.9 Cu.Ft, 900W)
products.verdict: 900W, a 0.9 cu ft cavity and 11 power levels. Faster, but check your dorm rules.
products.description:
The Toshiba lists 900W output, a 0.9 cu ft cavity and 11 power levels, in the $50 to $100 range. Higher wattage heats faster than the 700W picks, and a larger cavity gives room for full-size plates and bowls that crowd the smaller models.

It ranks last because 900W may exceed a dorm's wattage limit, and the bigger body needs more space on a shelf. A microwave that your housing office bans is worth nothing, regardless of how fast it heats.

Buy it for an off-campus apartment or a suite with no wattage limit. Skip it if your dorm caps wattage, and take a 700W pick instead. Confirm your school's policy first, because many dorms enforce the cap and may confiscate an oversized appliance.
cons: May exceed a dorm wattage limit
products.idealFor: Off-campus apartments and suites with no limit.

whatMatters.detail: Many housing offices cap appliance wattage, and 700W is a common ceiling. Look up your dorm's rule before buying, because a 900W unit like the Toshiba may be banned outright. If the policy is silent, email the housing office and ask, since a confiscated microwave is an expensive lesson. Keep the reply in writing so you can show it to a resident adviser if challenged.

A 0.7 cu ft microwave is compact but still needs real shelf width plus ventilation space. Measure your shelf or fridge top before ordering, and leave a few inches behind and above for airflow. Check the listing for outside dimensions, not only cavity size, since the two differ by several inches once the casing, door and handle are counted.

Beeps carry through thin dorm walls. A mute button silences them, and several models list one, including the COMFEE' and both Chefman units. The Farberware, Frigidaire and BLACK+DECKER do not. Check for the word mute on the listing, because it is the feature that keeps roommates friendly at night, and many listings bury it in the bullets.

In a shared room nobody reads the manual. Labeled presets and a few clear buttons beat a complicated panel. A child safety lock also stops accidental starts, which matters in a busy suite. Look at the control photos on the listing and count the buttons before you decide, since a panel with a dozen tiny keys invites mistakes.

whatMatters.factor: Check the cavity against your plate
whatMatters.detail: A 0.7 cu ft cavity fits a standard plate, but large bowls and wide plates can be tight, and a turntable that cannot spin freely cooks unevenly. If you reheat big meals, a bigger cavity helps, as long as your housing rules allow it. Compare cavity size to the dishes you own, and measure your largest bowl across.

faq.q: What wattage is allowed in a dorm?
faq.a: It varies by school, and 700W is a common limit. Check your housing rules before buying, and ask the office if the policy is unclear. Most picks here are 700W, and only the Toshiba is 900W, so the safest default is 700W.

For reheating and standard plates, yes. A 0.9 cu ft unit like the Toshiba gives more room, but it adds footprint and wattage. If your dishes are large, measure them against the 0.7 models first, because a turntable that cannot spin cooks unevenly.

faq.q: Which microwave has a mute button?
faq.a: The COMFEE' units and both Chefman microwaves list a mute function. The Farberware, Frigidaire and BLACK+DECKER do not, so choose one of the first group if you share a room and sleep on different schedules.

faq.q: Is the Pearl White COMFEE' worth the extra?
faq.a: Only for the color. The specs match the standard COMFEE', including the mute function, ECO mode and 700W output. Pay the premium only if white matters to your room, and expect to wipe it more often.

faq.q: Can I use a 900W microwave in a dorm?
faq.a: Maybe, but many dorms cap wattage and some enforce it. Ask your housing office before buying the Toshiba, and keep a written reply in case the question comes up later, since inspectors can remove appliances during room checks.

faq.q: Do I need a child lock?
faq.a: It stops accidental starts in a shared room. Both Chefman models and the Farberware list a child safety lock. It also helps if a visiting sibling touches the buttons, so it is a small but useful safeguard that costs nothing extra on those models.

finalTake: Buy the COMFEE' for a standard dorm, or the Chefman with presets if cooking is new to you. Choose the Farberware on the tightest budget and the Toshiba only if your housing allows 900W. Check your school's wattage cap and measure your shelf before ordering, because those two checks matter more than any feature.
